title: Water resources & management
examples: What causes water stress in a region?
How does a water transfer scheme work?
What are the environmental impacts of moving water?

explain.say: Today we will learn about water stress and management.

items: Water stress means not enough water.
Management means careful use of water.
Schemes are ways to move water.

explain.say: Water stress happens when demand is greater than supply.
Climate change can increase the frequency of droughts.
Water transfer schemes move water from one place to another.
A concrete example is moving river water to dry farmland.
In real life, cities use these schemes to supply drinking water.

faq.q: What is the difference between water scarcity and water stress?
faq.a: Water scarcity means there is simply not enough water available anywhere. Water stress is when the demand for water is greater than the available supply, even if some water exists.
asks: Is scarcity the same as stress?

faq.q: Are water transfer schemes always a good idea for the environment?
faq.a: Not always. They can damage ecosystems at the source and destination. Careful environmental assessment is needed before building them.
asks: What are the downsides of canals?

faq.q: What is the main cause of increased water demand?
faq.a: The main cause is often population growth combined with increased industrial use. Agriculture is also a huge user of water.

faq.q: How can we reduce water stress in our local area?
faq.a: We can adopt better water conservation practices everywhere. This includes fixing leaks and using water efficiently in gardens.
asks: How can people help with water shortages?

faq.q: What is meant by 'sustainable water management'?
faq.a: It means managing water in a way that meets current needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs. It balances human use with nature's needs.
asks: How do we keep water for the future?

facts: Water stress occurs when human demand exceeds available freshwater supply.
Droughts are long periods of abnormally low rainfall, affecting water sources.
Water transfer schemes use canals or pipelines to move water over long distances.
Sustainable management requires balancing human needs with environmental health.

quiz.say: If a region has high population growth and little rainfall, it is most likely experiencing:
quiz.why: Water stress happens when the need for water is higher than what is naturally available.

wrong.0: The water cycle describes how water moves naturally, not the human pressure on it.
wrong.2: This means there is too much water, which is the opposite of the situation described.
wrong.3: A drought is a symptom, but water stress describes the imbalance between need and supply.

quiz.say: What is the primary purpose of a water transfer scheme?
quiz.show: Goal: Move water from A to B

options.show: To supply water to an area facing scarcity.
options.say: To supply water to an area facing scarcity.

quiz.why: These schemes physically move water resources to where they are needed most.

wrong.0: Water transfer moves existing water; it cannot create rain where it does not fall.
wrong.2: Cleaning is done at treatment plants, not by moving the water itself.
wrong.3: While they can help manage impacts, they do not solve the root cause of climate change.

quiz.say: Which of these practices best represents sustainable water management?
quiz.show: Balancing use for people and planet

options.show: Diverting all river water to cities.
options.say: Diverting all river water to cities.

quiz.why: Rainwater harvesting uses a natural cycle resource locally, reducing strain on main sources.

wrong.1: Large dams can disrupt river ecosystems and are not always sustainable for all environments.
wrong.2: This creates dependency and ignores local conservation efforts.
wrong.3: This leaves no water for the rivers and the wildlife that depends on them.
